 JUDGMENT
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is taken up for final disposal.
The appellant/claimant is before this Court being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 03.03.2017 passed in MVC No.751/2012 on the file of II Addl.

Brief facts of the case are that;
On 18.07.2011 at 8.45 a.m. the petitioner was proceeding to his house by walk on the left hand side of the road from the area of Dalmadi Darga, located near Kurikota Bride of Kurikota village,
Gulbarga Taluk, on Gulbarga-Hamnabad road, at that time one Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-4/EW-9953 belonging to the respondent No.1 ridden by one NC:
2023:KHC-K:8581 Sharanappa came in rash and negligent manner and dashed the petitioner causing severe injuries to him over the head, shoulder, chest and other vital parts of the body.
Petitioner was shifted to Primary Health Centre, Kurikota and thereafter shifted to Basaveshwara Hospital, Gulbarga.
The doctor thereafter referred to higher treatment.
He was shifted to Ganga Institute of Neuroscience and Trauma Care, Solapur, where he was treated as in-patient and operated to injuries from 18.7.2011 to 25.7.2011.

Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
(b) Based on the pleadings, the tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence.
Claimant examined himself as PW.1 and exhibited 14 documents marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
Doctor-Rajendra Kothari has been examined as PW.2.
On behalf of the respondent No.2 one Anil Kumar Katke has been examined as RW.1 and exhibited 10 documents, marked as Ex.R1 to R10.

(c) On appreciation of pleadings and evidence tribunal held that the accident in question had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the Hero Honda motorcycle by its rider resulting in injuries to the NC: 2023:KHC-K:8581 claimant/petitioner and consequently held that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,27,500/-.

The tribunal further found that rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid driving license and as such there was a violation of term of policy and accordingly directed respondent No.1 to pay compensation exonerating the respondent No.2-Insurance Company from liability of paying the compensation.
Being aggrieved by the same appellant/claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
4. Heard.
Perused the records.
5. From the records it is clear that accident in question resulting in injuries to the appellant/petitioner is not in dispute.
Petitioner was aged about 22 years and carrying on work of Mason.
The tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- p.m.

In the absence of production of any material and even in terms of chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority NC: 2023:KHC-K:8581 the assessment of said income is justifiable and warrants Rukmanna vs Jagannath And Anr on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193549685/

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.55,987/- towards medical expense, same is maintained as it is.
Tribunal has awarded 'attendant's charge, food and conveyance' of Rs.19,000/- same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/- by adding 11,000/-.

Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards 'loss of amenities and nutrition food'
is added to Rs.10,000/- awarded by tribunal making it Rs.25,000/-.
Grant of compensation Rs.18,000/- towards 'loss of income during the period of treatment' is maintained as it is.

sentences.text: This Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra), has noticed the defences available to the Insurance Company under Section 149(2)(a)(ii) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The Insurance Company is entitled to take a defence that the offending vehicle was driven by an unauthorised person or the person driving the vehicle did not have a valid driving licence.

The onus would shift on the Insurance Company only after the owner of the offending vehicle pleads and proves the basic facts within his knowledge that the driver of the offending vehicle was authorised by him to drive the vehicle and was having a valid driving licence at the relevant time.

Rukmanna vs Jagannath And Anr on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193549685/
4 17.
This issue has been answered in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. (supra).

In that case, it was contended by the insurance company that once the defence taken by the insurer is accepted by the Tribunal, it is bound to discharge the insurer and fix the liability only on the owner and/or the driver of the vehicle.

However, this Court held that even if the insurer succeeds in establishing its defence, the Tribunal or the Court can direct the insurance company to pay the award amount to the claimant(s) and, in turn, recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
The three-Judge Bench, after analysing the earlier decisions on the point, held that there was no reason to deviate from the said well-settled principle".

Accordingly, even in the instant case since it is held that rider of the motorcycle did not have valid driving license, the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount in the first instance and thereafter recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.

10. For the foregoing reasons, following:
ORDER
a) The appeal is partly allowed.

b) The appellant/claimant is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.3,73,387/-
instead of Rs.3,27,500/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
However, appellant is not entitled to interest for the delayed period of 265 days in filing the appeal.

c) Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid compensation amount within an outer limit of six weeks from the date of receipt of certified - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8581 copy of this judgment and thereafter recover the same from respondent No.1.
d) The award of the Tribunal is modified accordingly.
